source.publication: 2025 Complete Income Tax Instruction Booklet (ip25), Kansas Department of Revenue, with Form K-40 and Schedule S bound in (PDF pages 19-22)
source.section: Form K-40 lines 1-12 (ip25 PDF page 20; exemption block PDF page 19); K-40 instructions lines 1-3 (PDF page 6), line 4 and exemptions (PDF page 6), lines 5-8 (PDF page 7); tax rate schedule: 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34) and Tax Table (PDF pages 27-34)

worked: Federal AGI = wages (you) 60,000.00 + wages (spouse) 45,000.00 = 105,000.00. Federal taxable income = 105,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 (31,500.00) = 73,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Kansas starts from federal AGI). No Kansas modifications: Schedule S lines A9 and A26 are 0.00, line A27 net modification 0.00 (the K-40 instructions let a filer skip line 2). Form K-40: line 1 federal AGI 105,000.00; line 2 modifications 0.00; line 3 Kansas AGI = 105,000.00 + (0.00) = 105,000.00; line 4 standard deduction (married filing joint) 8,240.00; line 5 exemption allowance (2 exemptions) 18,320.00, 0 dependents; line 6 total deductions = 8,240.00 + 18,320.00 = 26,560.00; line 7 taxable income = 105,000.00 - 26,560.00 = 78,440.00; line 8 tax (rate schedule as numbers, PDF page 34): 5.2% x 46,000.00 = 2,392.00 + 5.58% x (78,440.00 - 46,000.00 = 32,440.00) = 1,810.1520; total 4,202.1520 = 4,202.15. Line 7 is 100,000 or less, so the form reads the tax table: row 78,401-78,450, married filing joint column, PDF page 32, gives 4,201; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 9-10 do not apply (resident); line 11 0.00; line 12 total income tax 4,202.15. Credits (lines 13-15, 17): none, 0.00; state income tax = 4,202.15. Both spouses under 65: no worksheet box. Joint schedule: the 5.2% band runs to 46,000.
accepted_approximations: Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
